oneLiner: 我们更愿相信支持已有观点的证据，忽略反面信息。
oneLinerEn: We favor evidence that supports what we already believe and dismiss the rest.
detail: 表现：读新闻只挑认同的媒体、记起「我说过会这样」的预言而忘记落空的。为什么：大脑省能量，也保护自我认同。如何避免：主动寻找反面证据、把「我哪里可能错了」当作问题。
detailEn: How it shows: reading only like-minded media, recalling hits but forgetting misses. Why: the brain saves energy and protects identity. How to avoid: seek disconfirming evidence; ask 'where might I be wrong?'

oneLiner: 先看到的数字会拽住后续判断，哪怕它毫无关系。
oneLinerEn: The first number we see drags later judgments, even if irrelevant.
detail: 表现：原价划掉再标「特价」、谈判先开高价更占优。为什么：系统1被初始值锚住，调整不足。如何避免：先想「合理区间」再谈价，多方比价。
detailEn: How it shows: strike-through prices, opening high in negotiation. Why: System 1 sticks to the anchor and under-adjusts. How to avoid: set your own fair range first, compare across sources.

oneLiner: 容易想起的事，就被当成更常见的事。
oneLinerEn: What comes easily to mind feels more common.
detail: 表现：飞机失事刷屏后不敢坐飞机，却每天开车。为什么：记忆的鲜活度替代了真实频率。如何避免：用统计数据替代直觉印象。
detailEn: How it shows: fearing flying after a headline crash while driving daily. Why: vividness stands in for base rates. How to avoid: rely on statistics over impressions.

oneLiner: 亏 100 块的痛，约是赚 100 块的快的两倍。
oneLinerEn: The pain of losing 100 feels about twice the joy of gaining 100.
detail: 表现：死扛亏损股票、不愿换更优方案怕失去已有。为什么：进化上避损比逐利更关乎生存。如何避免：用「机会成本」提醒自己不行动也在损失。
detailEn: How it shows: holding losing stocks, refusing a better deal to avoid loss. Why: avoiding loss aided survival. How to avoid: weigh the cost of inaction too.

oneLiner: 越多人相信，越容易跟着信——哪怕人人都错。
oneLinerEn: The more people believe something, the likelier we follow—even if all are wrong.
detail: 表现：抢购、跟风投资、群体起哄。为什么：归属需求与「多数即正确」的捷径。如何避免：保留独立思考空间，先问「我自己信什么」。
detailEn: How it shows: panic buying, herd investing, mobbing. Why: need to belong and the shortcut 'majority = right'. How to avoid: keep space to think alone first.

oneLiner: 已经花掉、收不回的，不该影响接下来的决定。
oneLinerEn: Money or time already spent and unrecoverable shouldn't shape future choices.
detail: 表现：难看的电影看完才走、烂尾项目硬撑。为什么：不想承认「白花了」。如何避免：只问「从现在看，继续值不值」。
detailEn: How it shows: finishing a bad film, propping a failing project. Why: reluctance to admit waste. How to avoid: ask only 'is continuing worth it now?'

oneLiner: 一个人某方面出色，我们就以为他样样都行。
oneLinerEn: If someone excels at one thing, we assume they're good at everything.
detail: 表现：颜值高的人被认为更聪明可靠、名校生更易获信任。为什么：大脑用整体印象替代理性分项。如何避免：就事论事，分开评估不同能力。
detailEn: How it shows: attractive people judged smarter; elite alumni trusted more. Why: global impression substitutes for itemized judgment. How to avoid: evaluate traits separately.

oneLiner: 越不懂，越容易高估自己；越精通，越知不足。
oneLinerEn: The least skilled overestimate most; the most skilled underestimate.
detail: 表现：新手自信满满、专家却谨慎。为什么：能力低者也缺乏「识别自己不行」的能力。如何避免：把「我不懂」当起点，向做得好的人请教。
detailEn: How it shows: novices overconfident, experts cautious. Why: the unskilled also lack the skill to see it. How to avoid: treat 'I don't know' as a start; learn from better performers.

oneLiner: 解释他人行为时高估性格、低估情境，把偶然的失误当作本性。
oneLinerEn: We over-credit disposition and under-credit situation in others, reading a slip as character.
detail: 表现：别人迟到就认为他懒，自己迟到却怪交通。为什么：观察他人时情境不明显、行为显眼。如何避免：先问「换成我在那个处境会怎样」。
detailEn: Shows as: they're late so they're lazy, I'm late because of traffic. Why: the situation is hidden when we watch others. Avoid it by asking 'how would I act in their place?'

oneLiner: 事后总觉得『我早就知道会这样』，高估了自己事前的预测力。
oneLinerEn: Afterward we feel 'I knew it all along', overrating how predictable events were beforehand.
detail: 表现：结果一出就说股灾、比赛或选举早已写在脸上。为什么：新信息重塑了我们对旧预期的记忆。如何避免：事前写下预测，用记录对抗事后美化。
detailEn: Shows as: once the result is known, crashes or elections seem obvious. Why: new info rewrites memory of old expectations. Avoid it by logging predictions in advance.

oneLiner: 同一信息的不同表述（收益还是损失）会系统性地改变我们的选择。
oneLinerEn: The same facts, framed as gains or losses, systematically shift our choices.
detail: 表现：说『存活率 90%』比『死亡率 10%』更让人接受手术。为什么：损失比收益更刺痛，我们怕损失。如何避免：把同一选项用不同框架重写一遍再比较。
detailEn: Shows as: '90% survive' wins over '10% die' for the same surgery. Why: losses loom larger than gains. Avoid it by restating each option in the opposite frame.

oneLiner: 一旦拥有某物，我们对它的估值就高于未拥有时。
oneLinerEn: Once we own something, we value it higher than before we owned it.
detail: 表现：马克杯实验里拥有者索要价远高于买家愿付价；旧物舍不得卖。为什么：失去被当作损失，损失被放大。如何避免：假设自己从未拥有，问现在愿花多少去买。
detailEn: Shows as: owners demand far more for a mug than buyers will pay; we hoard old things. Why: giving up feels like a loss, and losses loom. Avoid it by asking what you'd pay to buy it now.
